moat_against: Largely undifferentiated distribution — low switching costs, no long-term contracts with many customers, intense Sysco/US Foods competition
Thin economics: gross margin 11.93% in FY2026, operating margin 1.31%; ROIC proxy 6.63% in FY2026, 6.14% in FY2025, 3.06% in FY2022
Supplier and product-cost inflation/deflation pass-through risk; fuel, labor and insurance cost exposure
Convenience mix depends in part on cigarettes/alternative nicotine, a structurally declining category
moat_for: #3 US food distributor — scale in procurement, logistics and route density smaller rivals cannot match
Independent-restaurant focus (43.1% of Foodservice sales in Q4 FY2026) with Performance Brands private label and higher-touch service
Diversified Convenience (Core-Mark) and Specialty (Vistar) segments peers cannot replicate in one house
Dense Southeast footprint deepened by Cheney Brothers (acquired Oct 2024)
moat_justification: Scale as the #3 US food distributor, route density and a differentiated Convenience business give moderate advantages, but the service is largely undifferentiated, margins are ~1.3% operating, customers/suppliers have power, and ROIC proxy has run only ~6-8% in FY2023-26 (3.06% in FY2022) with gross margin 10.33-11.93% over the last five years — not well above the cost of capital through a cycle.
name: Performance Food Group Company
one_liner: Solid #3 food distributor, moat 4/10 — does not clear 15% at $97.78 (weighted IRR 8.31%, weighted IV@15% $44.28); it clears 15% only below $44.28.
